verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:

verses.zh: 「你吩咐亚伦和他子孙说：要远离以色列人所分别为圣、归给我的圣物，免得亵渎我的圣名。我是耶和华。
verses.en: “Tell Aaron and his sons that they must deal respectfully with the holy offerings[NOTE:1] of the Israelites, which they consecrate to me, so that they do not profane my holy name.[NOTE:2] I am the Lord.
notes: Heb “holy things,” which means the “holy offerings” in this context, as the following verses show. The referent has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Heb “from the holy things of the sons of Israel, and they shall not profane my holy name, which they are consecrating to me.” The latter (relative) clause applies to the “the holy things of the sons of Israel” (the first clause), not the Lord’s name (i.e., the immediately preceding clause). The clause order in the translation has been rearranged to indicate this.
verses.commentary:
22:2 "be careful with the holy gifts" The subject of ceremonial purity continues. The priest must maintain
purity because

- if not he profanes YHWH's name, Lev. 22:2 (NIDOTTE, vol. 2, pp. 145-150; cf. Lev. 18:21; 19:12; 20:3; 21:6); see

SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT)

- if not he will be "cut off," Lev. 22:3; see full note at Lev. 7:20

The MT has "hold yourself away from the holy things." This VERB (BDB 634, KB 684, Niphal
IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense) means "to separate something/someone in
a ceremonial sense." The priests were to be very careful about how they handled sacrifices.

- right animal

- right place

- right person

- right time

- who at what, where, and when

- how to specifically handle the blood

- how to specifically dispose of the remains

These procedures were crucial to maintain "holiness."

▣

NASB, NRSV, TEV, LXX
"dedicate"

NKJV, NJB
"sanctify"

JPSOA
"consecrate"

REV, Peshitta (Lamsa)
"hallow"

This is the VERB form (Niphal IMPERFECT used in a
JUSSIVE sense) of the root "holy," "sacred," "apartness," "separated to" (BDB 871-3, KB 1073). It is
used six times in this chapter. The NASB translates it in two ways.

- "dedicate" ‒ Lev. 22:2,3

- "sanctify" ‒ Lev. 22:10,16,32 (twice)

See SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY.

▣ "so as not to profane" This VERB (BDB 320, KB 319, Piel
IMPERFECT, possibly another IMPERFECT, like "dedicate," used in a
JUSSIVE sense). This word for "pollute," "defile," or "profane" occurs several times in
Leviticus (cf. Lev. 18:21; 19:8,12,29; 20:3; 21:4,6,9,12,15,23; 22:2,9,15,32). It is the opposite of "holy."

▣ "My holy name" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: "THE NAME" OF YHWH (OT).

verses.zh: 你要对他们说：你们世世代代的后裔，凡身上有污秽、亲近以色列人所分别为圣、归耶和华圣物的，那人必在我面前剪除。我是耶和华。
verses.en: Say to them, ‘Throughout your generations,[NOTE:1] if any man from all your descendants approaches the holy offerings, which the Israelites consecrate[NOTE:2] to the Lord, while he is impure,[NOTE:3] that person must be cut off from before me.[NOTE:4] I am the Lord.
notes: Heb “To your generations.”
The Piel (v. 2) and Hiphil (v. 3) forms of the verb קָדַשׁ (qadash) appear to be interchangeable in this context. Both mean “to consecrate” (Heb “make holy [or “sacred”]”).
Heb “and his impurity [is] on him”; NIV “is ceremonially unclean”; NAB, NRSV “while he is in a state of uncleanness.”
Regarding the “cut off” penalty, see the note on Lev 7:20. Cf. the interpretive translation of TEV “he can never again serve at the altar.”
verses.commentary:
22:3 "I am the Lord" This is Israel's God covenant title ‒ YHWH. See
SPECIAL TOPIC: NAMES FOR DEITY, D.
It is repeated in Lev. 22:2, 3, 8, 9, 16, 30, 31,3 2, 33. YHWH's covenant people must keep His commandments (cf. Lev. 22:31;
see SPECIAL TOPIC: KEEP and
SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT.

▣ "uncleanness" This NOUN (BDB 380) is the focus of the chapter. As chapter 21 dealt
with the priest's family, this chapter deals with necessity of the "cleanness" of the priest (Lev. 22:4-7) and sacrifices (Lev. 22:8)
that are eaten.

verses.zh: 亚伦的后裔，凡长大麻疯的，或是有漏症的，不可吃圣物，直等他洁净了。无论谁摸那因死尸不洁净的物（或译：人），或是遗精的人，
verses.en: No man[NOTE:1] from the descendants of Aaron who is diseased or has a discharge[NOTE:2] may eat the holy offerings until he becomes clean. The one[NOTE:3] who touches anything made unclean by contact with a dead person,[NOTE:4] or with a man who has a seminal emission,[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “Man man.” The reduplication is a way of saying “any man” (cf. Lev 15:2; 17:3, etc.), but with a negative command it means “No man” (see B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 147).
The diseases and discharges mentioned here are those described in Lev 13-15.
Heb “And the one.”
Heb “in all unclean of a person/soul”; for the Hebrew term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) meaning “a [dead] person,” see the note on Lev 19:28.
Heb “or a man who goes out from him a lying of seed.”
verses.commentary:
22:4-9 Here is a list of what defiles a priest from eating sacrifices.

- leprosy (cf. Lev. 21:20; and chapter 13)

- a discharge

- one who touches something unclean

- a corpse

- seminal emission (cf. Lev. 15:1-18)

- teeming things (cf. Lev. 11:29-31)

The unclean priest must remain defiled until

- evening

- a bath (i.e., cleaned by water, cf. Lev. 11:24-25,28,32,40)

but then he may eat.

22:4 "No man" This is a Hebrew idiom, literally, "man, man" (cf. Lev. 15:2; 17:3; 22:18; and several more).

verses.zh: 或是摸甚么使他不洁净的爬物，或是摸那使他不洁净的人（不拘那人有甚么不洁净），
verses.en: or with a man who touches a swarming thing by which he becomes unclean,[NOTE:1] or who touches a person[NOTE:2] by which he becomes unclean, whatever that person’s impurity[NOTE:3]—
notes: Heb “which there shall be uncleanness to him.”
The Hebrew term for “person” here is אָדָם (ʾadam, “human being”), which could be either a male or a female person.

Heb “to all his impurity.” The phrase refers to the impurity of the person whom the man touches to become unclean (see the previous clause). To clarify this, the translation uses “that person’s” rather than “his.”
verses.commentary:
22:5

NASB
"teeming things"

NKJV, LXX, Peshitta
"creeping things"

NRSV, JPSOA
"swarming things"

TEV
"unclean animal"

NJB
"reptile"

REB
"creature"

The root (BDB 1056) denotes that which swarms in great numbers (i.e., Gen. 7:21; 8:17). In Leviticus
they are all classified as "unclean" (cf. Lev. 11:29-31,41-45,46-47).

All of these cause "uncleanness" (BDB 379, KB 375, cf. Lev. 22:5,6,8) by either

- touching them (Lev. 22:5-6)

- touching their dead bodies (cf. Lev. 5:2)

- eating them (cf. Deut. 14:19)

verses.zh: 摸了这些人、物的，必不洁净到晚上；若不用水洗身，就不可吃圣物。
verses.en: the person who touches any of these[NOTE:1] will be unclean until evening and must not eat from the holy offerings unless he has bathed his body in water.
notes: The phrase “any of these” refers back to the unclean things touched in vv. 4b-5.

verses.zh: 日落的时候，他就洁净了，然后可以吃圣物，因为这是他的食物。
verses.en: When the sun goes down he will be clean, and afterward he may eat from the holy offerings, because they are his food.

verses.zh: 自死的或是被野兽撕裂的，他不可吃，因此污秽自己。我是耶和华。
verses.en: He must not eat an animal that has died of natural causes[NOTE:1] or an animal torn by beasts and thus become unclean by it. I am the Lord.
notes: Heb “a carcass,” referring to the carcass of an animal that has died on its own, not the carcass of an animal slaughtered for sacrifice or killed by wild beasts. This has been clarified in the translation by supplying the phrase “of natural causes”; cf. NAB “that has died of itself”; TEV “that has died a natural death.”
verses.commentary:
22:8 As Lev. 22:4-7 defined the priest who may eat, 22:8 puts a restriction on the type of sacrifice that may
be eaten by priests (i.e., no animal that has died naturally or has been torn by other animals, cf. Lev. 11:39-40; 17:15).

verses.zh: 所以他们要守我所吩咐的，免得轻忽了，因此担罪而死。我是叫他们成圣的耶和华。
verses.en: They must keep my charge so that they do not incur sin on account of it[NOTE:1] and therefore die[NOTE:2] because they profane it. I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
notes: Heb “and they will not lift up on it sin.” The pronoun “it” (masculine) apparently refers to any item of food that belongs to the category of “holy offerings” (see above).
Heb “and die in it.”
verses.commentary:
22:9 "keep My charge" This VERB (BDB 1036, KB 1581) and NOUN (BDB 1038)
often appear together (cf. Lev. 18:30; Deut. 11:1; Josh. 22:3; Mal. 3:14). YHWH expects obedience!

▣ "die" The VERB "cut off" (BDB 503, KB 500) in Lev. 22:3 is defined as death in 22:9.
See full note at Lev. 7:30.

verses.zh: 「凡外人不可吃圣物；寄居在祭司家的，或是雇工人，都不可吃圣物；
verses.en: “‘No lay person[NOTE:1] may eat anything holy. Neither a priest’s lodger[NOTE:2] nor a hired laborer may eat anything holy,
notes: Heb “No stranger” (so KJV, ASV), which refers here to anyone other than the Aaronic priests. Some English versions reverse the negation and state positively: NIV “No one outside a priest’s family”; NRSV “Only a member of a priestly family”; CEV “Only you priests and your families.”

Heb “A resident [תּוֹשָׁב (toshav) from יָשַׁב (yashav, “to dwell, to reside”)] of a priest.” The meaning of the term is uncertain. It could refer to a “guest” (NIV) or perhaps “bound servant” (NRSV; see B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 149). In the translation “lodger” was used instead of “boarder” precisely because a boarder would be provided meals with his lodging, the very issue at stake here.
verses.commentary:
22:10-13 This paragraph delineates those people so closely connected to a priest's family that they can also
eat of the holy sacrifices.

- a sojourner living with a priest (see note at Lev. 22:10)

- a hired person of a priest (possibly non-Israelite)

- a slave of a priest

- the slave's children

- the priest's daughter who has been widowed or divorced (but not if she is married to a non-priest or has children of a
non-priest); for a good brief discussion of the place of the widow in ancient Israel, see NIDOTTE, vol. 1, pp. 413-414

22:10

NASB
"layman"

NKJV
"outsider"

NRSV, NJB, JPSOA, REB
"lay person"

TEV
"only a member of a priestly family"

LXX, Peshitta
"alien"

This PARTICIPLE (BDB 266, KB 267) denotes someone not of the tribe of Levi,
nor someone of the tribe of Levi but not a priest (cf. Exod. 29:33; 30:33; Lev. 22:10,12,13; Num. 1:51; 3:10; 18:7). It could
denote an Israelite of another tribe (cf. Lev. 22:12).

verses.zh: 倘若祭司买人，是他的钱买的，那人就可以吃圣物；生在他家的人也可以吃。
verses.en: but if a priest buys a person with his own money,[NOTE:1] that person[NOTE:2] may eat the holy offerings,[NOTE:3] and those born in the priest’s[NOTE:4] own house may eat his food.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “and a priest, if he buys a person, the property of his silver.”
Heb “he”; the referent (the person whom the priest has purchased) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “eat it”; the referent (the holy offerings) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “his”; the referent (the priest) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

Heb “and the [slave] born of his house, they shall eat in his food.” The LXX, Syriac, Tg. Onq., Tg. Ps.-J., and some mss of Smr have plural “ones born,” which matches the following plural “they” pronoun and the plural form of the verb.

verses.zh: 祭司的女儿若嫁外人，就不可吃举祭的圣物。
verses.en: If a priest’s daughter marries a lay person,[NOTE:1] she may not eat the holy contribution offerings,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And a daughter of a priest, if she is to a man, a stranger” (cf. the note on v. 10 above).

Heb “she in the contribution of the holy offerings shall not eat.” For “contribution [offering]” see the note on Lev 7:14 and the literature cited there. Cf. NCV “the holy offerings”; TEV, NLT “the sacred offerings.”

verses.zh: 但祭司的女儿若是寡妇，或是被休的，没有孩子，又归回父家，与她青年一样，就可以吃她父亲的食物；只是外人不可吃。
verses.en: but if a priest’s daughter is a widow or divorced, and she has no children so that she returns to live in[NOTE:1] her father’s house as in her youth,[NOTE:2] she may eat from her father’s food, but no lay person may eat it.
notes: Heb “to”; the words “live in” have been supplied in the translation for clarity.

Heb “and seed there is not to her and she returns to the house of her father as her youth.” The mention of having “no children” appears to imply that her children, if she had any, should support her; this is made explicit by NLT’s “and has no children to support her.”

verses.zh: 若有人误吃了圣物，要照圣物的原数加上五分之一交给祭司。
verses.en: “‘If a man eats a holy offering by mistake,[NOTE:1] he must add one-fifth to it and give the holy offering to the priest.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And a man, if he eats a holy thing in error” (see the Lev 4:2 note on “straying,” which is the term rendered “by mistake” here).

When a person trespassed in regard to something sacred to the Lord, reparation was to be made for the trespass, involving restitution of that which was violated plus one-fifth of its value as a fine. It is possible that the restoration of the offering and the additional one-fifth of its value were made as a monetary payment (see, e.g., B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 150). See the regulations for the “guilt offering” in Lev 5:16; 6:5 [5:24 HT] and the notes there.
verses.commentary:
22:14 "unintentionally" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: UNINTENTIONAL SINS. Here, it denotes "by accident" (cf. Lev. 5:14-16). But even so, he must add
a fifth more and give it back to a priest. This is part of the "guilt offerings" (cf. Lev. 5:16).

This verse is also addressing the "layman" or "sojourner."

verses.zh: 祭司不可亵渎以色列人所献给耶和华的圣物，
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] must not profane the holy offerings which the Israelites contribute[NOTE:2] to the Lord,[NOTE:3]
notes: Contextually, “They” could refer either to the people (v. 14a; cf. NRSV “No one”) or the priests (v. 14b; cf. NIV “The priests”), but the latter seems more likely (see J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 356, and B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 150). The priests were responsible to see that the portions of the offerings that were to be consumed by the priests as prebends did not become accessible to the people. Mistakes in this matter (cf. v. 14) would bring “guilt” on the people, requiring punishment (v. 16).
The Hebrew verb הֵרִים (herim, rendered “contribute” here) is commonly used for setting aside portions of an offering (see, e.g., Lev 4:8-10 and R. E. Averbeck, NIDOTTE 4:335-36).

Heb “the holy offerings of the sons of Israel which they contribute to the Lord.” The subject “they” here refers to the Israelites (“the sons of Israel”) which is the most immediate antecedent. To make this clear, the present translation has “the holy offerings which the Israelites contribute to the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
22:15 "them" In context this must refer to "the priests" (i.e., who offered the sacrifices to YHWH), not the
"layman" of 22:14.

verses.zh: 免得他们在吃圣物上自取罪孽，因为我是叫他们成圣的耶和华。」
verses.en: and so cause them to incur a penalty for guilt[NOTE:1] when they eat their holy offerings,[NOTE:2] for I am the Lord who sanctifies them.’”
notes: Heb “iniquity of guilt”; NASB “cause them to bear punishment for guilt.” The Hebrew word עָוֹן (ʾavon, “iniquity”) can designate either acts of iniquity or the penalty (i.e., punishment) for such acts.
That is, when the lay people eat portions of offerings that should have been eaten only by priests and those who belonged to priestly households.
verses.commentary:
22:16 The PRONOUNS of Lev. 22:16 are ambiguous. The context has been addressing two people.

- priests

- non-priest Israelites

▣ "I am the Lord who sanctifies them" This is recurrent theme. Israel is holy
because their God is holy (cf. Lev. 11:44; 19:2; 20:7,26). These guidelines in Leviticus are meant to maintain that holiness.

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：
verses.en: The Lord spoke to Moses:
verses.commentary: 22:17-25 This deals with freewill/peace offerings connected to the fulfillment of a vow (cf. Leviticus 3).

verses.zh: 「你晓谕亚伦和他子孙，并以色列众人说：以色列家中的人，或在以色列中寄居的，凡献供物，无论是所许的愿，是甘心献的，就是献给耶和华作燔祭的，
verses.en: “Speak to Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites and tell them, ‘When any man[NOTE:1] from the house of Israel or from the resident foreigners[NOTE:2] in Israel presents his offering for any of the votive or freewill offerings, which they present to the Lord as a burnt offering,
notes: Heb “Man, man.” The reduplication is a way of saying “any man” (cf. Lev 15:2; 17:3, etc.; see the distributive repetition of the noun in GKC 395-96 §123.c).
Heb “foreigner [singular].” Some medieval Hebrew mss, Smr, LXX, Syriac, and Vulgate add “who resides”: “the foreigner who resides in Israel” (cf., e.g., Lev 20:2 above).
verses.commentary:
22:18 Notice two distinct groups are addressed.

- Israelites

- non-Israelites living among them (i.e., sojourners, aliens, cf. Lev. 16:29)

verses.zh: 要将没有残疾的公牛，或是绵羊，或是山羊献上，如此方蒙悦纳。
verses.en: if it is to be acceptable for your benefit,[NOTE:1] it must be a flawless male from the cattle, sheep, or goats.
notes: Heb “for your acceptance.” See Lev 1:3-4 above and the notes there.
verses.commentary:
22:19 "for you to be accepted" This has no VERB. With the NOUN
(BDB 953; NIDOTTE, vol. 3, pp. 1186-1188), it is often hard to know when YHWH

- accepts a sacrifice on behalf of a person (cf. Lev. 19:5)

- accepts the person into fellowship (i.e., Lev. 1:4; 7:18)

The root is repeated several times in this chapter.

- the NOUN (cf. Lev. 22:19,20,21,29)

- the VERB (BDB 953, KB 1980, Niphal IMPERFECT, cf. Lev. 22:23,25,27)

verses.zh: 凡有残疾的，你们不可献上，因为这不蒙悦纳。
verses.en: You must not present anything that has a flaw,[NOTE:1] because it will not be acceptable for your benefit.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “all which in it [is] a flaw.” Note that the same term is used for physical flaws of people in Lev 21:17-24. Cf. KJV, ASV, NRSV “blemish”; NASB, NIV, TEV “defect”; NLT “with physical defects.”
Heb “not for acceptance shall it be for you”; NIV “it will not be accepted on your behalf” (NRSV and NLT both similar).

verses.zh: 凡从牛群或是羊群中，将平安祭献给耶和华，为要还特许的愿，或是作甘心献的，所献的必纯全无残疾的才蒙悦纳。
verses.en: If a man presents a peace-offering sacrifice to the Lord for a special votive offering[NOTE:1] or for a freewill offering from the herd or the flock, it must be flawless to be acceptable;[NOTE:2] it must have no flaw.[NOTE:3]
notes: The meaning of the expression לְפַלֵּא־נֶדֶר (lefalleʾ neder) rendered here “for a special votive offering” is much debated. Some take it as an expression for fulfilling a vow, “to fulfill a vow” (e.g., HALOT 927-28 s.v. פלא piel and NASB; cf. NAB, NRSV “in fulfillment of a vow”) or, alternatively, “to make a vow” or “for making a vow” (HALOT 928 s.v. פלא piel [II פלא]). Perhaps it refers to the making a special vow, from the verb פָלַא (palaʾ, “to be wonderful, to be remarkable”); cf. J. Milgrom, Numbers (JPSTC), 44. B. A. Levine, Leviticus (JPSTC), 151 and 193, suggests that this is a special term for “setting aside a votive offering” (related to פָּלָה [palah, “to set aside”]). In general, the point of the expression seems to be that this sacrifice arises as a special gift to God out of special circumstances in the life of the worshiper.
Heb “for acceptance”; NAB “if it is to find acceptance.”
Heb “all/any flaw shall not be in it.”

verses.zh: 瞎眼的、折伤的、残废的、有瘤子的、长癣的、长疥的都不可献给耶和华，也不可在坛上作为火祭献给耶和华。
verses.en: “‘You must not present to the Lord something blind, or with a broken bone, or mutilated, or with a running sore,[NOTE:1] or with a festering eruption, or with a feverish rash.[NOTE:2] You must not give any of these as a gift[NOTE:3] on the altar to the Lord.
notes: Or perhaps “a wart” (cf. NIV; HALOT 383 s.v. יַבֶּלֶת, but see the remarks in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 358).
See the note on Lev 21:20 above.
This term for offering “gift” is explained in the note on Lev 1:9.
verses.commentary:
22:22-25 This lists the defects that are not acceptable. They are like the defects that eliminate Levites from
being a functioning priest (cf. Lev. 21:16-20). The offering and the offerer, as well as the ones who eat it,
are to be "clean," without defect. It was a visible sign of the perfection of YHWH.

For the lexical aspect of these defects, see Leviticus 21.

verses.zh: 无论是公牛是绵羊羔，若肢体有余的，或是缺少的，只可作甘心祭献上；用以还愿，却不蒙悦纳。
verses.en: As for an ox[NOTE:1] or a sheep with a limb too long or stunted,[NOTE:2] you may present it as a freewill offering, but it will not be acceptable for a votive offering.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “And an ox.”
Heb “and stunted” (see HALOT 1102 s.v. I קלט).

The freewill offering was voluntary, so the regulations regarding it were more relaxed. Once a vow was made, the paying of it was not voluntary (see B. A. Levine, Leviticus [JPSTC], 151-52, for very helpful remarks on this verse).
verses.commentary:
22:23 Notice the exception related to freewill offerings. This shows there were "levels" of "cleanness" or "holiness."

The PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, "too long" (BDB 976, KB 1358), occurs only here
and in Lev. 21:18. The PASSIVE PARTICIPLE, "too short" (BDB 886, KB 2102), occurs only here.

verses.zh: 肾子损伤的，或是压碎的，或是破裂的，或是骟了的，不可献给耶和华，在你们的地上也不可这样行。
verses.en: You must not present to the Lord something with testicles that are bruised, crushed, torn, or cut off;[NOTE:1] you must not do this in your land.
notes: Cf. Lev 21:20b.
verses.commentary:
22:24 This has been understood as outlawing the castration of animals (Targums, Josephus, Antiq. 4.8.40)
in Israel. This may be another distinction between Israel and her pagan neighbors.

verses.zh: 这类的物，你们从外人的手，一样也不可接受作你们　神的食物献上；因为这些都有损坏，有残疾，不蒙悦纳。」
verses.en: Even from a foreigner[NOTE:1] you must not present the food of your God from such animals as these, for they are ruined and flawed;[NOTE:2] they will not be acceptable for your benefit.’”
notes: Heb “And from the hand of a son of a foreigner.”

Heb “for their being ruined [is] in them, flaw is in them”; NRSV “are mutilated, with a blemish in them”; NIV “are deformed and have defects.” The MT term מָשְׁחָתָם (moshkhatam, “their being ruined”) is a Hophal participle from שָׁחַת (shakhat, “to ruin”). Smr has plural משׁחתים בהם (“deformities in them”; cf. the LXX translation). The Qumran Leviticus scroll (11QpaleoLev) has תימ הם[…], in which case the restored participle would appear to be the same as Smr, but there is no ב (bet) preposition before the pronoun, yielding “they are deformed” (see D. N. Freedman and K. A. Mathews, The Paleo-Hebrew Leviticus Scroll, 41 and the remarks in J. E. Hartley, Leviticus [WBC], 358).

verses.commentary:
22:32 "sanctified. . .sanctifies" This is the root kadosh (BDB 872, KB 1073; see
SPECIAL TOPIC: HOLY). It is used several
times in Leviticus 21-22 as a NOUN, an ADJECTIVE, and a VERB. Here
are some of the different ways it is translated.

- holy, most holy

- sacred

- sanctify

- dedicate

- consecrate

- hallowed

Holiness is "the" key theological concept in Leviticus. Remember, it is the "how to" manual for the
Tabernacle. It gives the guidelines on how a holy God can fellowship with an unholy people. Their holiness
is mandated and facilitates the fellowship with YHWH.

22:33 This is an allusion to YHWH's great act of promise (cf. Gen. 15:12-22) and mercy (i.e., the exodus).
This is covenant language (cf. Lev. 11:45; 19:36; 22:33; 25:38; 26:45). The Feast of Passover was a way
to remind and educate future Israelites of YHWH's great act of deliverance!

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Brief outline

- Be careful about the "cleanness" of

- the priests, Lev. 22:3-9

- who can eat the sacrifices, Lev. 22:10-16h

- acceptable sacrifices, Lev. 22:17-25,26-30

- Concluding statement, Lev. 22:2 and 30-33

- Notice that the defects in priests mentioned in chapter 21 are matched in chapter 22 by defects in animals (Lev. 22:17-25).

- This ceremonial defilement seems so strange to moderns but remember, this is the ANE and "holiness" is the key
theological issue of the book.

- Only priests in the Tabernacle could eat that which is "most holy" but the priest and his family (cf. Leviticus 7) could eat
some sacrifices (cf. Leviticus 6-7).

- grain offerings (except for the small part offered on the altar)

- tithes

- right thighs

- peace offerings

- firstlings

Also, the person of the tribe of Levi who could not function as a priest because of the deformities
or accidents listed in Leviticus 21, could still eat of the holy gifts.

- Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, p. 417, suggests that there were three kinds of communal sacrifices.

- the sacrifice of praise (todah, cf. Lev. 7:12-15; 22:29-30)

- the voluntary sacrifice from one's devotion (nedabah, cf. Lev. 7:16-17; 22:18-23)

- the votive sacrifice (nedar, cf. Lev. 7:16-17; 22:18-23)

All of these are addressed in Leviticus 3.
